---
title: "Session 3: Data Visualization and Reporting with Quarto"
---

## Theme

Communicating actuarial results.

This session teaches the final part of the mini-project workflow: choosing clear charts, writing plain-language interpretation, rendering a Quarto report, and saving the processed dataset.

## Learning Outcomes

At the end of this session, participants will be able to:

- Produce effective visualisations using `ggplot2`.
- Select appropriate graphics for actuarial summaries and comparisons.
- Integrate narrative, code, tables, and figures within Quarto.
- Generate a reproducible HTML report.
- Present actuarial findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Publish the completed project to GitHub.

## Case Study Milestone

Participants reproduce Sections 5 and 6 of the mini-project:

- Create reusable plots for product, claim type, and risk-band summaries.
- Explain what each chart shows.
- Save `data/processed/portfolio_clean.csv`.
- Render the final Quarto report.

## Suggested Timing

| Time | Activity |
|---:|---|
| 20 min | Chart choice for actuarial communication |
| 30 min | Distribution, comparison, and risk profile charts |
| 25 min | Tables and narrative in Quarto |
| 25 min | Mini-project report completion |
| 15 min | AI report review |
| 5 min | Wrap-up |

## Core Code From The Mini-Project

```{r}
#| eval: false

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

ggplot(summary_by_product, aes(x = product, y = loss_ratio)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#C05621") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Loss ratio by product",
    x = "Product",
    y = "Loss ratio"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

write_csv(portfolio, "data/processed/portfolio_clean.csv")
```

## AI Checkpoint

Use AI to review the report for clarity, chart choice, and possible unsupported conclusions. Keep only suggestions that are supported by the actual data and analysis.
